seoDescription: Learn to play "Hey Jealousy" by Gin Blossoms with this comprehensive guitar lesson. This tutorial breaks down every section of the classic track, covering both electric guitar parts in detail. You'll master the main riff, the verse chord voicings, and the strumming patterns. The lesson also dives into the chorus octaves, pre-solo clean chords, and a note-for-note breakdown of the iconic guitar solo, complete with double stops, pentatonic runs, and country-style bends.

chapters.title: Introduction and Tone Setup
chapters.description: The lesson begins with an introduction to the song and a guide to achieving the right overdrive and clean guitar tones.

chapters.title: Main Riff: Guitar 1
chapters.description: Learn the first guitar's main riff, including the D5 to E to F# minor chord progression and the specific strumming pattern.

chapters.title: Main Riff: Guitar 2
chapters.description: This chapter covers the second guitar's part for the main riff, featuring longer ringing chords and a unique F# voicing.

chapters.title: Verse Guitar Parts
chapters.description: This section breaks down the two complementary guitar parts for the verse: a clean, arpeggiated line and a palm-muted rhythm part.

chapters.title: Chorus: Guitar 1 (Octaves)
chapters.description: Learn to play the first guitar's chorus part, which uses a melodic line built from octaves and a staccato rhythm.

chapters.title: Chorus: Guitar 2 (Chords)
chapters.description: This chapter covers the second guitar's powerful rhythm part for the chorus using A, D5, and F# minor chords.

chapters.title: Pre-Solo Clean Arpeggios
chapters.description: A quick look at the clean, high-fretted arpeggios that are played just before the guitar solo begins.

chapters.title: Solo Breakdown: Melodic Runs and Double Stops
chapters.description: The first section of the solo is broken down, focusing on the initial slide, pentatonic runs, and double-stop phrases.

chapters.title: Solo Breakdown: Rhythmic Muting and Bends
chapters.description: Learn the funky, percussive muted section of the solo and the country-rock style bends that immediately follow.

chapters.title: Solo Breakdown: Final Licks and Outro
chapters.description: This final chapter details the last phrases of the solo, featuring more bends and double stops, and concludes the lesson.

summary:
## Guitar Tone
- **Overdrive**: Use an overdrive pedal for the main riffs and the solo to get the right amount of grit. The lesson uses a Great Eastern Effects Designer Drive.
- **Clean**: A simple, clean amp tone is needed for the verse sections.

## Main Riff
> [!IMPORTANT]
The song features two distinct, complementary guitar parts for most sections.

- **Guitar 1 (Rhythm Focus)**
  - **Progression**: D5 - E - F# minor - E.
  - **Fill**: A lick on the G string (frets 4-6-4), often played as a double stop.
  - **Strumming**: A core pattern of `down, down, up` on the first chord, followed by `up, down, down, up` after the change.
- **Guitar 2 (Melodic Layer)**
  - Follows the same chord progression but lets the chords ring out longer.
  - Uses an **F# chord with the open B and E strings** for a fuller, more jangly sound.

## Verse Sections
- **Guitar 1 (Clean Part)**: Plays a clean, arpeggiated part using a sliding D5 shape, an E major shape, and an F# minor voicing that incorporates the open high E string.
- **Guitar 2 (Rhythm Part)**: Plays a simple, driving rhythm with **palm-muted** D, E, F#, and E power chords.

## Chorus Sections
- **Guitar 1 (Octaves)**: This part is built entirely on **octaves**, creating a melodic line that moves between the 12th, 9th, 7th, and 5th frets. It's played with a staccato, rhythmic feel.
- **Guitar 2 (Power Chords)**: Provides the harmonic foundation with a powerful chord progression.
  - **Progression 1**: A to D5.
  - **Progression 2**: F# minor to D5.
  - **Strumming**: Features aggressive strumming with muted string "whacks" for percussive effect.

## Guitar Solo Breakdown
> [!TIP]
The solo is a masterclass in melodic phrasing, blending pentatonic runs with country-inspired techniques.

1.  **Opening**: The solo kicks off with a long slide on the G string from the 2nd to the 14th fret.
2.  **Melodic Phrases**: It continues with meandering **pentatonic** lines mixed with melodic single-note runs.
3.  **Texture**: **Double stops** and slides are used frequently to add thickness and movement to the lines.
4.  **Rhythmic Break**: A funky section features percussive, muted string "squeezes" for a rhythmic effect.
5.  **Bends**: The solo is famous for its **country-style bends**, including phrases where you pick additional notes while a bend is held.
